title: Your Turn My Turn poster
lede: April Greiman’s 3-D poster for a furniture design symposium at the Pacific Design Center: red and cyan type, dot screens, and wedges in a tilted, layered field.
summary: Tilted “Your Turn My Turn” in red and cyan offsets, dot-screen panels, yellow wedges, and a spaced “1 9 8 3”. April Greiman, 1983.

source.label: People’s Graphic Design Archive: Your Turn My Turn, Pacific Design Center event

made: 1983 (People’s Graphic Design Archive; the poster is dated © 1983)

evidence.note: Inspected the People’s Graphic Design Archive image (1440 × 2188), a flat photograph of one copy; the owner is not stated. Not stored.

styles.note: Clear example. It has almost every trait in the rubric: tilted and stepped lines, dot screens, overlapping layers, wedges and bars, and spaced numerals.

context: The People’s Graphic Design Archive lists the poster as offset lithography, 24 × 36 in, for PDC2 Pacific Design Center / Westweek, and says it was a 3-D poster issued with glasses. [People’s Graphic Design Archive](https://peoplesgdarchive.org/item/738/your-turn-my-turn-pacific-design-center-event), [second record](https://peoplesgdarchive.org/item/1422/your-turn-my-turn-3-d-poster).
The poster names the event “The International Contract Furniture Design Symposium during WestWeek”, 18 and 19 March, Pacific Design Center, Los Angeles.
observed: “Your Turn” and “My Turn” are set in a heavy italic grotesque at a slight tilt, each letter printed twice in dark red and cyan with an offset, as in anaglyph 3-D.
Small copies of “turn” and “you” float upside down and mirrored around the main words.
A panel of coarse dark-red dot screen fills the upper left. A field of red, white, and cyan spray dots spreads over a dark panel at the right.
Yellow and blue wedges and a black diagonal band cross the sheet. A red-grey photograph of the Earth sits at the lower left.
“1  9  8  3” is set as separate numerals stepping up across the dark panel.
Sponsor lists are set small on a yellow panel at an angle; the event details at the lower left are flush left in blue and pink italics, each line stepped to the right.
“P D C 2” sits in small separate squares at the top left.
interpretation: The poster shows how Greiman’s California work adds colour and depth to Weingart’s structure: the dot screens and wedges stay, but the palette moves to cyan, pink, and yellow, and the overprint becomes a literal 3-D effect.
borrow: Print a display word twice in two colours with a small offset.
Space out a year into single numerals that step across a panel.
Tilt a small-print list as a block and keep its lines parallel to the panel edge.

rights.statement: No image is stored. April Greiman is living, so the design is in copyright. The photograph’s owner is not stated.
